chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Sabih, from Anbasa al-Abid, who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away while fasting Sha'ban and Ramadan, and three days of every month: the first Thursday, the middle Wednesday, and the last Thursday; and Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon them) used to fast those days.

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: Three days (referring to the white days or specific days of fasting)
key_terms.صَوْمُ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَعْبَانَ: Fasting of the month of Sha'ban
key_terms.قُبِضَ: Passed away / Taken (in a state of)

ai.seo_question: What was the fasting practice of the Prophet and the Imams regarding the three days of each month?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) consistent practice of fasting the three white days (Ayyam al-Beed) alongside his voluntary fasts in Sha'ban and Ramadan, a tradition meticulously preserved by the Imams Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon them). In Shia scholarship, this serves as a key evidence for the continuity of Sunnah through the Imams, emphasizing the spiritual merit of regular voluntary fasting as a means of spiritual purification and closeness to God. The specific timing—often associated with the full moon—underscores the cosmic and rhythmic nature of worship in Islamic tradition.
